title: Founded in 1992
summary: The Premier League broke away from the Football League First Division to form its own competition.
detail: The FA Premier League began in 1992 with 22 clubs (later 20). It became the most-watched domestic football league in the world, built on a new domestic TV deal.

title: 38-match season
summary: Each of the 20 clubs plays every other club home and away — 380 fixtures in total.
detail: Unlike World Cup knockouts, the Premier League is a pure double round-robin. Points decide the champion, European places, and the three relegated clubs.

title: Three points for a win
summary: England adopted three points for a win in 1981; the Premier League kept the rule from day one.
detail: A win is worth three points, a draw one, and a loss zero. Goal difference then goals scored break ties before any play-off scenarios.

title: Relegation and promotion
summary: The bottom three drop to the Championship; three clubs come up each summer.
detail: Promotion keeps the league competitive across eras. Newly promoted clubs often fight for survival while established big six sides chase Europe.

title: European places
summary: Top-four clubs usually qualify for the Champions League; cups can reshuffle Europa and Conference slots.
detail: England's strong UEFA coefficient has added Champions League spots in some seasons. Domestic cups (FA Cup, League Cup) also feed European berths.

title: Invincibles
summary: Arsenal went unbeaten across the entire 2003–04 Premier League season.
detail: Arsène Wenger's Arsenal side finished 26–12–0. No Premier League club has matched a full unbeaten title season since.

title: 100-point City
summary: Manchester City set the points record with 100 in 2017–18.
detail: Pep Guardiola's City won 32 matches and scored 106 goals that season, rewriting the modern points standard for a 38-game campaign.

title: Golden Boot tradition
summary: The season's top scorer wins the Golden Boot — often shared when tallies finish level.
detail: Icons from Shearer and Henry to Salah and Haaland have topped the charts. Assists have a parallel award: the Playmaker.

title: Boxing Day football
summary: A packed festive fixture list is a Premier League tradition rarely matched abroad.
detail: Clubs often play on Boxing Day and again days later, turning December into one of the season's toughest scheduling stretches.

title: Global audience
summary: Matches are broadcast in more than 200 territories worldwide.
detail: Morning kickoffs in England are prime time across Asia and late nights in the Americas — a key reason the league became a global sports product.

title: VAR era
summary: Video Assistant Referee reviews arrived in the Premier League in 2019–20.
detail: VAR checks goals, penalties, direct red cards, and mistaken identity. Offside technology and semi-automated systems continue to evolve the process.

title: Anfield noise
summary: Liverpool's Anfield is famous for "You'll Never Walk Alone" before big nights.
detail: Atmosphere is part of the Premier League product. Historic grounds and modern stadiums alike shape how title races feel on television and in person.
